abstract.text:
Generalized uncertainty principle puts forward the existence of the shortest distances and/or maximum momentum at the Planck scale for consideration. In this article, we investigate the solutions
of a two-dimensional Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau (DKP) oscillator within an external magnetic field in
a minimal length (ML) scale. First, we obtain the eigensolutions in ordinary quantum mechanics.
Then, we examine the DKP oscillator in the presence of an ML for the spin-zero and spin-one
sectors. We determine an energy eigenvalue equation in both cases with the corresponding eigenfunctions in the non-relativistic limit. We show that in the ordinary quantum mechanic limit, where
the ML correction vanishes, the energy eigenvalue equations become identical with the habitual
quantum mechanical ones. Finally, we employ the Euler-Mclaurin summation formula and obtain
the thermodynamic functions of the DKP oscillator in the high-temperature scale.

evidence.quote: We show that in the ordinary quantum mechanic limit, where the ML correction vanishes, the energy eigenvalue equations become identical with the habitual quantum mechanical ones.

replications.why: The paper checks that removing the minimal-length correction recovers established quantum-mechanical energy results.

evidence.quote: Instead of following that ansatz, we examine the spin-one case in another formalism as given in [38–40].

targets.why: It avoids a prior ansatz that made the spin-one case equivalent to the spin-zero case without physical justification.

evidence.quote: In this article, we investigate the solutions of a two-dimensional Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau (DKP) oscillator within an external magnetic field in a minimal length (ML) scale.

thesis.text: The paper solves a two-dimensional Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau oscillator under an external magnetic field in minimal-length quantum mechanics and uses the resulting spin-zero spectrum to compute high-temperature thermodynamic functions.

evidence.quote: Thermal properties of a two-dimensional Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau oscillator under an external magnetic field in the presence of a minimal length
Houcine Aounallah,1, ∗ Bekir Can Lütfüoğlu,2, 3, † and Jan Křı́ž3, ‡

identity.title: Thermal properties of a two-dimensional Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau oscillator under an external magnetic field in the presence of a minimal length

evidence.quote: Our main motivation is to obtain the modification of the thermodynamic functions.
We expect that the introduction of the external magnetic field with the existing of the ML will present important consequences on the thermal properties of the DKP oscillator.

question.text: How do an external magnetic field and a minimal length modify the energy spectrum and high-temperature thermodynamic functions of a two-dimensional DKP oscillator, especially for spin-zero and spin-one sectors? The hypothesis is that introducing the external magnetic field together with the minimal length will have important consequences on the thermal properties of the DKP oscillator.

sections.summary: The paper introduces its goal: studying a two-dimensional DKP oscillator under an external magnetic field in a minimal-length (ML) setting, with emphasis on deriving energy spectra and thermodynamic functions. It motivates the work through GUP, DKP, and thermal-property literature and identifies a gap in statistical treatments.
sections.title: Introduction: GUP, DKP, and thermal motivation

sections.summary: Reviews the DKP equation in flat space-time, its β-matrix algebra, and the irreducible representations used for spin-zero and spin-one particles: 5×5 matrices for scalar particles and 10×10 matrices for vector particles.
sections.title: DKP equation and irreducible representations

sections.summary: Formulates the spin-zero DKP oscillator with non-minimal coupling to an external magnetic field in ordinary quantum mechanics. It derives the coupled equations, reduces them to a radial equation in momentum polar coordinates, obtains the energy spectrum via confluent hypergeometric functions, and gives the non-relativistic limit.
sections.title: Spin-zero DKP oscillator in ordinary quantum mechanics

sections.summary: Treats the spin-one DKP oscillator in ordinary quantum mechanics using the 10×10 representation. It notes the difficulty of the coupled equations, rejects a prior simplifying ansatz as too particular, develops an alternative vector-scalar formalism, and finds that the non-relativistic spin-one spectrum differs from the spin-zero case.
sections.title: Spin-one DKP oscillator in ordinary quantum mechanics

sections.summary: Introduces the modified Heisenberg algebra for minimal length, applies it to the spin-zero DKP oscillator in momentum space, transforms the differential equation à la Jana et al., solves via hypergeometric functions, and obtains the ML-corrected energy spectrum and its non-relativistic limit.
sections.title: Minimal-length spin-zero DKP oscillator

sections.summary: Extends the minimal-length analysis to the spin-one DKP oscillator in the non-relativistic limit. It follows the same Jana et al. transformation strategy, derives ML-corrected energy eigenvalues, and verifies that the β=0 limit recovers the ordinary quantum mechanical result.
sections.title: Minimal-length spin-one DKP oscillator in the non-relativistic limit

sections.summary: Computes the canonical partition function for the spin-zero DKP oscillator ensemble at high temperature using the Euler-Maclaurin summation formula. It expands in the ML parameter to first order and derives Helmholtz free energy, entropy, internal energy, and specific heat expressions.
sections.title: Thermal properties: partition function and thermodynamic functions

sections.summary: Discusses the β=0 and zero-magnetic-field limits of the thermodynamic functions, identifies a critical temperature below which the Euler-Maclaurin high-temperature treatment breaks down, and interprets the plotted behavior of free energy, entropy, internal energy, and specific heat for different ML and magnetic-field values.
sections.title: OQM limits, critical temperature, and thermodynamic behavior

source_span.end_text: the Euler-MacLaurin approach starts to be valid.

sections.summary: Concludes the study by recapping the ordinary-quantum-mechanics treatment, the alternative spin-one approach, the ML-corrected energy spectrum, and the high-temperature thermodynamic results. It highlights the lower critical temperature for validity of the Euler-Maclaurin approximation and the role of the external magnetic field.
sections.title: Conclusion

sections.summary: Bibliography of cited works on GUP, DKP, relativistic oscillators, thermal properties, and related mathematical methods.
sections.title: References

sections.summary: Figure captions for the low-temperature Helmholtz free energy and the high-temperature thermodynamic functions (free energy, entropy, internal energy, specific heat) for β=0, 0.005, and 0.5.
sections.title: Figures: thermodynamic plots

type.reason: The paper presents original theoretical derivations and thermodynamic analysis for a two-dimensional DKP oscillator model, rather than reviewing existing literature.
